before.title: Planar dielectric interface with prescribed free surface charge
before.statement:
Let the laboratory frame, coordinates $(x,y,z)$ and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $S=\{z=0\}\cap\Omega$ be a stationary planar interface with unit normal $n=e_z$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-=\{z<0\}$ to the side $\Omega_+=\{z>0\}$. Suppose each half-space carries a homogeneous linear dielectric at rest in the laboratory frame in the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]]: constants $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\in(0,\infty)$ with $D=\varepsilon_1E$ on $\Omega_-$ and $D=\varepsilon_2E$ on $\Omega_+$. Let $E,B,D,H$ satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] in a neighbourhood of $S$ with a constant free surface charge density $\sigma_f\in\mathbb R$ and free surface current $K_f=0$. Write $E_{j\,t}$, $E_{j\,n}$ for the tangential and normal parts of the one-sided trace $E_j$ and $D_j$ ($j=1$ on $\Omega_-$, $j=2$ on $\Omega_+$), defined by the Euclidean decomposition against $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:
(a) [Tangential field] $n\times[E]=0$, i.e. $E_{2t}=E_{1t}$: the tangential electric field is continuous across the interface.
(b) [Normal displacement] $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$, i.e. $\varepsilon_2E_{2n}-\varepsilon_1E_{1n}=\sigma_f$, hence $E_{2n}=\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2}E_{1n}+\frac{\sigma_f}{\varepsilon_2}$.
(c) [No free sheet charge] If $\sigma_f=0$, then $\varepsilon_2E_{2n}=\varepsilon_1E_{1n}$ and $E_{2n}=\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2}E_{1n}$: the normal component is scaled by the positive ratio $\varepsilon_1/\varepsilon_2$, so $E_{2n}$ and $E_{1n}$ have the same sign; $E_{2n}=E_{1n}$ exactly when $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2$. A free surface charge $\sigma_f\ne0$ modifies the normal condition as displayed and is not silently set to zero.
(d) [Magnetic companions] $n\cdot[B]=0$ and, with $K_f=0$, $n\times[H]=0$; for nonmagnetic media with $H=\mu_0^{-1}B$ on both sides this gives $B_{2n}=B_{1n}$ and $B_{2t}=B_{1t}$.
(e) [Scope] A local interface computation under the stated model hypotheses: it solves the electric jump relations against the linear constitutive relations on the two sides and asserts no global field configuration, no existence of the fields, no constitutive law beyond the declared branch and no empirical claim.
before.strategy: **Proof technique:** substitute the constitutive relations into the jump identities of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]. (a)-(b): the theorem gives $n\times[E]=0$ and $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$ pointwise on $S$; decomposing $E_j=E_{j\,t}+E_{j\,n}\,n$ and using $D_j=\varepsilon_jE_j$ from [[post-em-material-closure]] (with the constant scalars $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2>0$) yields the displayed scalar relations, and solving the second for $E_{2n}$ is division by the positive constant $\varepsilon_2$. (c): set $\sigma_f=0$ in (b). (d): the remaining two identities of the theorem; in the nonmagnetic case $H=\mu_0^{-1}B$ on both sides, so $n\times[H]=0$ reads $n\times[B]=0$. The tangential/normal decomposition uses [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) records the scope. Only the jump theorem, the declared constitutive branch and elementary algebra are used.

after.title: Planar dielectric interface with prescribed free surface charge
after.statement:
Let the laboratory frame, coordinates $(x,y,z)$ and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $S=\{z=0\}\cap\Omega$ be a stationary planar interface with unit normal $n=e_z$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-=\{z<0\}$ to the side $\Omega_+=\{z>0\}$. Suppose each half-space carries a homogeneous linear dielectric at rest in the laboratory frame in the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]]: constants $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\in(0,\infty)$ with $D=\varepsilon_1E$ on $\Omega_-$ and $D=\varepsilon_2E$ on $\Omega_+$. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $E,B,D,H$ be locally integrable, $C^1$ off the plane and jointly one-sided $C^1$ up to it on every compact test cylinder, as in the joint branch of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]. Assume locally the four distributional macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], with volume sources $\rho_v,J_v$ continuous off the plane and locally integrable across it, free charge $\rho_f=\rho_v+\sigma_f\delta_S$ for a constant $\sigma_f\in\mathbb R$, and free current $J_f=J_v$ (no free sheet current). Here the plane distribution is defined locally by $\langle\delta_S,\psi\rangle=\int\psi(x,y,0,t)\,dx\,dy\,dt$ for compactly supported tests on the laboratory region; no global compactness of this plane is asserted. These are the local planar counterparts of the compact-interface hypotheses in [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]. Write $E_{j\,t}$, $E_{j\,n}$ for the tangential and normal parts of the one-sided trace $E_j$ and $D_j$ ($j=1$ on $\Omega_-$, $j=2$ on $\Omega_+$), defined by the Euclidean decomposition against $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:
(a) [Tangential field] $n\times[E]=0$, i.e. $E_{2t}=E_{1t}$: the tangential electric field is continuous across the interface.
(b) [Normal displacement] $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$, i.e. $\varepsilon_2E_{2n}-\varepsilon_1E_{1n}=\sigma_f$, hence $E_{2n}=\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2}E_{1n}+\frac{\sigma_f}{\varepsilon_2}$.
(c) [No free sheet charge] If $\sigma_f=0$, then $\varepsilon_2E_{2n}=\varepsilon_1E_{1n}$ and $E_{2n}=\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2}E_{1n}$: the normal component is scaled by the positive ratio $\varepsilon_1/\varepsilon_2$, so $E_{2n}$ and $E_{1n}$ have the same sign (and vanish together). Precisely, $E_{2n}=E_{1n}$ if and only if $(\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_2)E_{1n}=0$: equality holds when the normal field is zero even for unequal permittivities; if $E_{1n}\ne0$, it holds exactly when $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2$. A free surface charge $\sigma_f\ne0$ modifies the normal condition as displayed and is not silently set to zero.
(d) [Magnetic companions] $n\cdot[B]=0$ and, with $K_f=0$, $n\times[H]=0$; for nonmagnetic media with $H=\mu_0^{-1}B$ on both sides this gives $B_{2n}=B_{1n}$ and $B_{2t}=B_{1t}$.
(e) [Scope] A local interface computation under the stated model hypotheses: it solves the electric jump relations against the linear constitutive relations on the two sides and asserts no global field configuration, no existence of the fields, no constitutive law beyond the declared branch and no empirical claim.
after.strategy: **Proof technique:** local compact-test interface integration by parts, followed by substitution of the constitutive relations. The generally noncompact plane is not substituted into a globally compact-interface theorem. On each compact test cylinder, split the $z$ integral at zero; [[thm-integration-by-parts]] applied to the one-sided continuously differentiable factors on each side gives $\partial_z F_j=\{\partial_zF_j\}+[F_j]\delta_S$, while tangential derivatives have no sheet term. The compact-support integrands and their piecewise derivatives are bounded on the two closed half-cylinders and integrable; [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] therefore integrates these identities over $x,y,t$ and gives $\operatorname{div}F=\{\operatorname{div}F\}+e_z\cdot[F]\delta_S$ and $\operatorname{curl}F=\{\operatorname{curl}F\}+e_z\times[F]\delta_S$. Joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity bounds all regular terms locally, and time differentiation at this fixed plane contributes no sheet term. Insert these formulas into the assumed four distributional equations. To isolate a continuous sheet coefficient, test with a fixed tangential/time test times a rescaled normal cutoff supplied by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], equal to one at zero and supported in $|z|<h$; the regular difference terms are locally integrable (field derivatives are locally bounded, and volume sources are locally integrable), so their integrals tend to zero as $h\to0$ by [[thm-dominated-convergence]], dominated by their absolute values on a fixed compact cylinder; the plane is a volume-null set, whereas the sheet pairing is unchanged. Thus the four continuous coefficients agree pointwise. This proves the local identities $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$, $n\cdot[B]=0$, $n\times[E]=0$, $n\times[H]=0$, with precisely the signs of the compact-interface theorem. (a)-(b): in particular $n\times[E]=0$ and $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$ pointwise on $S$; decomposing $E_j=E_{j\,t}+E_{j\,n}\,n$ and using $D_j=\varepsilon_jE_j$ from [[post-em-material-closure]] (with the constant scalars $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2>0$) yields the displayed scalar relations, and solving the second for $E_{2n}$ is division by the positive constant $\varepsilon_2$. (c): set $\sigma_f=0$ in (b); subtract $E_{1n}$ to obtain $E_{2n}-E_{1n}=((\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_2)/\varepsilon_2)E_{1n}$. Since $\varepsilon_2>0$, its vanishing is exactly the displayed product condition; division by $E_{1n}$ is permitted only in the nonzero branch. (d): the remaining two local identities just proved; in the nonmagnetic case $H=\mu_0^{-1}B$ on both sides, so $n\times[H]=0$ reads $n\times[B]=0$. The tangential/normal decomposition uses [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) records the scope. Only the jump theorem, the declared constitutive branch and elementary algebra are used.

before.title: Uniform-field dielectric sphere: candidate solution and its class
before.statement:
Let the laboratory frame and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], with spatial coordinates $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, $z=x_3$, $r=|x|$ and the applied field along $e_3$. Fix $a>0$, a field magnitude $E_0>0$ and constants $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\in(0,\infty)$ (the interior and exterior permittivities of the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]], the material being at rest in the laboratory frame), and put $$C:=\frac{3\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}},\qquad d:=\frac{E_0a^3(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}})}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}.$$ Consider the time-independent potentials $$\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}(x):=-C\,E_0\,z\quad(r<a),\qquad \varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x):=-E_0\,z+\frac{d\,z}{r^3}\quad(r>a),$$ with fields $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ and $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}E$ inside, $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}E$ outside ($E$ being of the class of [[def-em-fields]] restricted to this time-independent configuration). Write $S=\{r=a\}$ and $n=e_r$ for the outward normal. Then:
(a) [Harmonicity] $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ on $r<a$ and $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ on $r>a$ in the classical sense of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and the potentials and their first derivatives extend continuously to the closed sides of $S$.
(b) [Interface conditions] With one-sided traces at $r=a$, $\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $S$; equivalently the tangential field is continuous and the normal component of $D$ is continuous, so the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] hold along $S$ in the time-independent reading with $\sigma_f=0$.
(c) [Asymptotics] $\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x)+E_0z=dz/r^3$ and $\nabla(\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z)=O(r^{-3})$ as $r\to\infty$: the difference from the applied uniform potential decays like $r^{-2}$ and its gradient like $r^{-3}$.
(d) [Uniqueness in the declared class] Let $(\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}},\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}})$ be $C^2$ on the closed ball $\overline{B_a}$ respectively on every closed exterior region $\{a\le r\le R\}$, harmonic on $r<a$ and $r>a$, satisfying the same interface conditions (b), and satisfying $|\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z|\le M/r$ for some $M$ and all sufficiently large $r$. Then $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$. Hence the displayed pair is the unique solution of the dielectric-sphere transmission problem in that class, existence being exhibited explicitly; the uniqueness proof uses only the Green identity, the matching conditions and the decay, with no maximum principle.
(e) [Fields, polarisation and induced dipole] On $r<a$ the field is uniform, $E=C E_0e_3$ with $D=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}CE_0e_3$; outside, the field is that of the applied uniform field plus the field of a point dipole at the origin with moment $p=4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,d\,e_3$; the interior polarisation is $P_{\mathrm{in}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_0)CE_0e_3$ and the bound surface charge density on $S$ is $\sigma_b=n\cdot(P_{\mathrm{in}}-P_{\mathrm{out}})$, the singular coefficient of $\rho_b=-\operatorname{div}P$ at $S$ (with the exterior polarisation $P_{\mathrm{out}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}-\varepsilon_0)E_{\mathrm{out}}$).
(f) [Regime and scope] The computation is a quasistatic result of the declared linear branch at $\sigma_f=0$; using $p$ as a dynamic wave polarisability of the sphere requires a separate quasistatic/dipole approximation and is not asserted here. The example asserts no material data and no empirical claim.

The linear system has determinant $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}>0$ and the displayed solution, so the interface equations hold; the equivalence with the jump conditions uses $E=-

initial_draft_before.title: Uniform-field dielectric sphere: candidate solution and its class
initial_draft_before.statement:
Let the laboratory frame and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], with spatial coordinates $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, $z=x_3$, $r=|x|$ and the applied field along $e_3$. Fix $a>0$, a field magnitude $E_0>0$ and constants $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\in(0,\infty)$ (the interior and exterior permittivities of the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]], the material being at rest in the laboratory frame), and put $$C:=\frac{3\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}},\qquad d:=\frac{E_0a^3(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}})}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}.$$ Consider the time-independent potentials $$\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}(x):=-C\,E_0\,z\quad(r<a),\qquad \varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x):=-E_0\,z+\frac{d\,z}{r^3}\quad(r>a),$$ with fields $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ and $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}E$ inside, $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}E$ outside ($E$ being of the class of [[def-em-fields]] restricted to this time-independent configuration). Write $S=\{r=a\}$ and $n=e_r$ for the outward normal. Then:
(a) [Harmonicity] $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ on $r<a$ and $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ on $r>a$ in the classical sense of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and the potentials and their first derivatives extend continuously to the closed sides of $S$.
(b) [Interface conditions] With one-sided traces at $r=a$, $\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $S$; equivalently the tangential field is continuous and the normal component of $D$ is continuous, so the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] hold along $S$ in the time-independent reading with $\sigma_f=0$.
(c) [Asymptotics] $\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x)+E_0z=dz/r^3$ and $\nabla(\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z)=O(r^{-3})$ as $r\to\infty$: the difference from the applied uniform potential decays like $r^{-2}$ and its gradient like $r^{-3}$.
(d) [Uniqueness in the declared class] Let $(\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}},\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}})$ be $C^2$ on the closed ball $\overline{B_a}$ respectively on every closed exterior region $\{a\le r\le R\}$, harmonic on $r<a$ and $r>a$, satisfying the same interface conditions (b), and satisfying $|\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z|\le M/r$ for some $M$ and all sufficiently large $r$. Then $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$. Hence the displayed pair is the unique solution of the dielectric-sphere transmission problem in that class, existence being exhibited explicitly; the uniqueness proof uses only the Green identity, the matching conditions and the decay, with no maximum principle.
(e) [Fields, polarisation and induced dipole] On $r<a$ the field is uniform, $E=C E_0e_3$ with $D=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}CE_0e_3$; outside, the field is that of the applied uniform field plus the field of a point dipole at the origin with moment $p=4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,d\,e_3$; the interior polarisation is $P_{\mathrm{in}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_0)CE_0e_3$ and the bound surface charge density on $S$ is $\sigma_b=n\cdot(P_{\mathrm{in}}-P_{\mathrm{out}})$, the singular coefficient of $\rho_b=-\operatorname{div}P$ at $S$ (with the exterior polarisation $P_{\mathrm{out}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}-\varepsilon_0)E_{\mathrm{out}}$).
(f) [Regime and scope] The computation is a quasistatic result of the declared linear branch at $\sigma_f=0$; using $p$ as a dynamic wave polarisability of the sphere requires a separate quasistatic/dipole approximation and is not asserted here. The example asserts no material data and no empirical claim.
